title: 1961 AHSME Problem 8
statement: Let the two base angles of a triangle be \(A\) and \(B,\) with \(B\) larger than \(A.\) The altitude to the base divides the vertex angle \(C\) into two parts, \(C_1\) and \(C_2,\) with \(C_2\) adjacent to side \(a.\) Then:

solutions.text:
The two right triangles give \[ \begin{aligned} A+C_1&=90^\circ,\\ B+C_2&=90^\circ. \end{aligned} \] Subtracting the second relation from the first gives \(C_1-C_2=B-A.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The altitude creates two right triangles
Express each part of \(C\) as a complement of the opposite base angle
